requirements.ask_text: Could you please tell me your date of birth?

source.text: 1. Security questions in this order: `date_of_birth`, `phone_last4`. Question wording and formats unchanged. / `date_of_birth` — ask for your date of birth. Format date, sent as YYYY-MM-DD; a date given only as numbers is read day, then month, then year.

requirements.ask_text: Could you please tell me the last 4 digits of your phone number?

source.text: `phone_last4` — ask for your phone last4. Format digits, exactly 4 digits including leading zeros.

identity.failed_instruction: Please use the mobile app or visit a branch.

source.text: 2 wrong answers in total end the check (was 3). / the API's `wrong_answers_left` is the count to use. / After 3 wrong answers, do not state the debt. Say "Please use the mobile app or visit a branch." and close as `id-fail` / `exhausted`. / If the customer declines to answer or asks what the call is about before answering, explain once that the questions protect their account. A second refusal closes as `id-fail` / `would-not-answer`. / Ask once more; if it is still unclear after the second ask, close as `no-contact` / `unclear`.

4. Callbacks: next business day only, never today. / A callback is for today or the next business day, from 12:00 to 19:00, both included, and later than `now`. Call `schedule_callback` with the date and the time, then close as `no-contact` / `cb-set`. If the person names a time outside that window, say so and ask once more. If no valid time results, close as `no-contact` / `cb-none`.

third_party.deceased_sentence: I am sorry for your loss.

source.text: Someone other than the customer (relative, colleague, friend): say nothing about the purpose. Ask when the customer can be reached. / Wrong number: apologise and close as `no-contact` / `wrong-no`. The customer has died: say "I am sorry for your loss." and close as `no-contact` / `deceased`.

Use the call variable `now` as the clock, never the machine clock. Business days are Monday to Saturday, except Bank 17 holidays: 2026-10-14, 2026-10-15. "Next <weekday>" means that weekday of the following week, even when today is that weekday; "this <weekday>" means the coming one.

| 1 to 3 | band1 | the third business day after today | 1 | / Attempt 1: propose the full past-due amount on the last business day of this week; if today is that day, the last business day of next week. If the customer already said the full amount is too much, attempt 1 proposes the floor instead.

2. Days late 4–60: the deadline is the last calendar day of the current month; if that day is not a business day, the next business day (no longer the sixth business day). / | 4 to 60 | band2 | ... | 1 |

Ask for the full past-due amount first. Never ask "how much can you pay?". Any amount between the floor and the full amount is accepted; an amount below the floor is refused, and the floor is offered once per product with the words "the rest stays overdue".

A promise date must be today or later, a business day, and not after the deadline. A weekend day or holiday rolls to the next business day. A vague date (next week, when I get paid): ask once for the exact day; if none follows, propose the deadline. A date after the deadline: offer the deadline instead.

special_cases.name: already_paid
special_cases.trigger: The customer says they have already paid the product.
special_cases.say: Payments can take one business day to appear.

source.text: Already paid: say "Payments can take one business day to appear.". Note the product as `already-paid` and continue with the other products.

special_cases.name: dispute
special_cases.trigger: The customer disputes the debt: says it is not their debt, they never had the product, or it was closed or paid off before.

source.text: Dispute (not their debt, never had the product, closed or paid off before): note the product as `disputes` and continue with the other products.

special_cases.name: hardship
special_cases.trigger: The customer mentions hardship such as illness, a death in the family or job loss.
special_cases.say: I am sorry to hear that.

source.text: Hardship (illness, a death in the family, job loss): say one short sentence of sympathy, make no persuasion attempt, and offer a transfer to the `welfare` team. If they accept, call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `welfare` and close as `escalated` / `welfare`. If they decline, close as `no-ptp` / `vulnerable`. A customer in hardship may still name a date and amount; record it.

special_cases.name: restructuring
special_cases.trigger: The customer asks for a payment plan, lower instalments or a change to the terms.

source.text: Restructuring (a payment plan, lower instalments, changing the terms): call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `plans` and close as `escalated` / `plans`. Promises already recorded on this call stay recorded.

special_cases.name: human
special_cases.trigger: The customer asks to speak to a human agent.

source.text: 4. ... Human requests: ask once whether you can help first. (7 Oct, overrides rule 29 "do not ask whether you can help") / A request for a human agent during the identity check: call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `front-desk` and close as `escalated` / `agent`.

special_cases.name: scam
special_cases.trigger: The customer suspects the call is a scam.
special_cases.say: You can verify this call by phoning Bank 17's customer service number.

source.text: If the person suspects a scam: say they can verify the call by phoning Bank 17's customer service number, and continue.

special_cases.name: robot
special_cases.trigger: The customer asks whether they are talking to a robot.

source.text: If asked whether this is a robot: say "I am Bank 17's digital assistant."
The customer refuses to talk: close as `no-ptp` / `refuses`.

special_cases.name: change_promise
special_cases.trigger: The customer asks whether a recorded promise can be changed.
special_cases.say: You can change it in the mobile app.

source.text: If the customer asks whether a recorded promise can be changed: say "You can change it in the mobile app."

table.when: A transfer, with the transfer's reason, even after a promise.
No promise: reason of the first product in get_account order that is not paid.

source.text: Thank the customer and say goodbye before `close_call`, which is the last tool call. / At least one promise recorded: `ptp-recorded`. A transfer: `escalated` with the transfer's reason, even after a promise. All products already paid: `already-paid`. No promise: `no-ptp` with the reason of the first product in `get_account` order that is not paid. / When the attempts for a product are used up without a promise, that product gets no promise and is noted `refuses`.

Before closing a call that is not a transfer, add exactly one note (`add_note`) for each product without a promise, with the reason that applies: `refuses`, `vulnerable`, `disputes`, `already-paid`, `tool-error`. No notes on a transfer.

`get_account` returns up to 3 products. State every product with its past-due amount and days late, all before asking anything; then ask once whether they can pay all of it today. / Every product is handled on the same call: a common date is checked against each product's own deadline and clamped to it; one read-back covers all pending promises; a transfer after a recorded promise keeps the promise.

phrases.opening: This is the automated assistant of Bank 17, and this call is recorded.
phrases.debt_intro: I am calling from the Bank 17 collections team about a late payment.
phrases.all_today_question: Can you pay all of it today?
phrases.scam_reply: You can verify this call by phoning Bank 17's customer service number.
phrases.after_promise_sentence: You will receive a text message confirming this promise.
phrases.already_paid_sentence: Payments can take one business day to appear.
phrases.recorded_promise_change_reply: You can change it in the mobile app.

source.text: First sentence: say you are the automated assistant of Bank 17 and that the call is recorded. Then ask whether you are speaking with the customer, using title and last name. / Before the identity check is complete, never say the words collections, debt, payment, credit card or loan, and do not say why you are calling. / After verification say you are calling from the Bank 17 collections team about a late payment. ... then ask once whether they can pay all of it today. / After a successful write say "You will receive a text message confirming this promise." / `mortgage` (say "mortgage") ... `student_loan` (say "student loan")

Correction to Operations' message of 7 October, point 3 only: after a failed create_promise the agent must NOT retry; the service-error outcome applies after the first failure. / Read the product, the amount and the date back and ask "Do you confirm?". Call `create_promise` only after a clear yes; one promise per product.

unresolved.text: verify_identity can return hint day_month_swapped, but the documents do not say what to tell the customer when it does.
The documents give no sentence for questions the assistant cannot answer.

Operations (7 Oct) say 'Human requests: ask once whether you can help first' without limiting it; rule 15 (transfer to front-desk during the identity check) predates it. The ask-once rule has been applied to every human request.
Rule 32 requires saying the promise could not be recorded (no dictated wording); the schema has no phrase field for it.
